name: HeterogeneousWorkerPool
purpose: Route inference tasks across mixed CPU+GPU workers with observed queue-depth + latency health, capability gating, and session-stickiness.
api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
import asyncio
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Generic, Literal, Protocol, TypeVar, runtime_checkable

R = TypeVar('R')
WorkerKind = Literal['cpu', 'gpu']

@dataclass
class Task(Generic[R]):
    payload: object
    session_id: str | None = None

@runtime_checkable
class HeterogeneousWorkerPool(Protocol[R]):
    def register(self, worker_id: str, capabilities: frozenset[str], kind: WorkerKind, executor: Callable[[Task[object]], Awaitable[R]]) -> None: ...
    def submit(self, task: Task[R], family: str) -> 'asyncio.Future[R]': ...
    def on_result(self, worker_id: str, latency_ms: float, ok: bool) -> None: ...

invariants.rule: A task with family=F MUST land on a worker advertising F in its capabilities.
GPU workers preferred when any healthy GPU worker has queue_depth < pool median; fallback CPU otherwise.
A worker whose rolling p50 latency over the last 100 samples is >= 2.0x pool-wide rolling p50 is deprioritized (weight 0.1x) within 30 seconds.
Session-stickiness: same session_id routes to same worker while worker healthy; on unhealthy, fails over.
Burst of N tasks spreads such that no single worker's queue exceeds 1.5x pool median.
Once a worker's rolling p50 normalizes back within 1.5x pool p50, full weight is restored within 30 seconds.

extension_contract: Rolling-window (50 samples) and unhealthy window (30s) are internal defaults overridable by subclassing. Routing algorithm itself is sealed; a different algorithm is a different primitive. A distributed Ray ActorPool adapter fits the same Protocol.
consumption_example:
pool = InMemoryHeterogeneousWorkerPool()
pool.register('gpu-a', frozenset({'llm-7b'}), 'gpu', gpu_exec)
fut = pool.submit(Task(payload={'prompt':'x'}), family='llm-7b')
result = await fut
why_essential: Without heterogeneous-aware routing, GPU workers sit idle on CPU-compatible tasks or overflow while CPU workers starve; static weights cannot track model warm-cache or worker health in real time.
alternatives_considered: Round-robin: ignores per-worker health/queue; a slow GPU starves throughput.
Static weight table: cannot react to hot-loaded models or cache advantages.
Single-kind homogeneous pool: wastes GPU headroom when CPU tasks could absorb load.
